notes: Reviewed accounting cases (reliability plan phase 5, 24 Oct 2026). Each case states the expected figures (must_contain), acceptable alternative wordings (must_contain_any / must_contain_groups), what a wrong answer would show (must_not_contain), citation expectations, and, with no_accounting_findings, that the answer must pass the treatment checks of app/orchestration/accounting_validation.py. Every expected figure is recomputed with Decimal arithmetic by tests/test_accounting_eval_set.py. Status 'proposed': the expectations were written by the engineering assistant and need an accountant's sign-off before this set gates a release. The 11 'prov-' cases (US GAAP and PCAOB, added 27 Oct 2026 from the 25 Oct answer review) are marked provisional individually: no authorised FASB or PCAOB evidence is held, so their expectations are not source-verified and must not be read as evidence coverage until a qualified accountant approves them.

cases.question: A UK VAT-registered business buys supplies for £6,000 including VAT at the standard rate of 20%. How much input VAT can it reclaim?
cases.conclusion: The VAT within a VAT-inclusive amount is one-sixth at 20%: £1,000, not 20% of £6,000.

cases.question: A UK business sells goods for £10,000 excluding VAT at the standard rate of 20%. What output VAT does it charge, and what does the customer pay?
cases.conclusion: Output VAT £2,000; the customer pays £12,000.

cases.question: A UK shop's takings for the day are £1,440 including VAT at 20%. How much is VAT and how much are net sales?
cases.conclusion: VAT £240 (one-sixth); net sales £1,200.

cases.question: In a VAT quarter a UK business has sales of £120,000 excluding VAT and purchases of £60,000 including VAT, all standard-rated at 20%. What VAT does it pay to HMRC?
cases.conclusion: Output VAT £24,000; input VAT £10,000 (one-sixth of £60,000); VAT payable £14,000.

cases.question: Record the journal entry for a credit sale of £5,000 plus VAT at 20% by a UK VAT-registered business.
cases.conclusion: Dr Trade receivables £6,000; Cr Sales £5,000; Cr Output VAT (VAT payable) £1,000.

cases.question: A company's corporation tax charge for the year is £36,000, payable nine months after the year end. Give the journal entries at the year end and on payment.
cases.conclusion: Year end: Dr Tax expense, Cr Corporation tax payable £36,000. On payment: Dr Corporation tax payable, Cr Cash £36,000.

cases.question: A company's year ends on 31 December. Its £3,000 electricity bill for December arrives and is paid in January. Record the entries.
cases.conclusion: 31 Dec: Dr Electricity expense, Cr Accruals £3,000. January: Dr Accruals, Cr Cash £3,000.

cases.question: On 1 October a company pays £12,000 rent for the next 12 months. Its year ends on 31 December. How much is rent expense for the year, and how much is prepaid at the year end?
cases.conclusion: Expense £3,000 (three months); prepayment £9,000.

cases.question: Under US GAAP ASC 842, a lessee has an operating lease with annual payments of $50,000 in arrears for 5 years and a 6% discount rate. What is the initial lease liability and the year-1 lease expense?
cases.conclusion: Lease liability $210,618.19 (present value of the payments); a single straight-line lease expense of $50,000 a year.

cases.question: Under IFRS 16, a lessee leases equipment with annual payments of $50,000 in arrears for 5 years at a 6% discount rate. What are the year-1 depreciation and interest?
cases.conclusion: Right-of-use asset and liability $210,618.19; depreciation $42,123.64; interest $12,637.09; total year-1 expense $54,760.73.

cases.question: Compare lessee accounting for leases under IFRS 16 and ASC 842.
cases.conclusion: IFRS 16 has a single lessee model (depreciation plus interest; no operating-lease classification for lessees, short-term and low-value exemptions aside); ASC 842 keeps finance and operating leases, with a single straight-line cost for operating leases.

cases.question: What is the present value of £10,000 received in 3 years at a discount rate of 5% a year?
A £200,000 loan at 6% a year is repaid monthly over 25 years. What is the monthly payment?
Revenue rose from £480,000 to £552,000. What is the percentage increase?

cases.question: Convert $2,500 to pounds at an exchange rate of £1 = $1.25.

Net income is $1,000,000 and 500,000 shares are outstanding all year. Convertible bonds pay $60,000 interest a year, the tax rate is 25%, and they convert into 50,000 shares. What are basic and diluted EPS?
cases.conclusion: Basic $2.00; incremental $0.90 per share (dilutive); diluted $1,045,000 ÷ 550,000 = $1.90.

cases.conclusion: No tax treatment without the jurisdiction and the kind of taxpayer: Kriton asks, or states the assumption it makes.

cases.question: Explain this comparison with a grounded example. Context: what is tax
cases.conclusion: A worked example whose treatment agrees with its explanation: VAT within VAT-inclusive amounts, VAT a liability not a cost, the tax expense recognised against a payable.

cases.topic: US GAAP cloud computing implementation costs
cases.question: Software Development Costs – Cloud Computing Arrangements (ASC 350-40). On January 1, 2026, Core Platform Inc. begins developing an internal-use cloud platform and enters into a hosting arrangement that is a service contract. During 2026 it incurs: preliminary project stage (evaluating alternatives) $80,000; coding and hardware configuration for the application development stage $450,000; data conversion from the old system $60,000; training $40,000. 1. Determine the costs capitalised versus deferred as a prepaid asset. 2. Provide the journal entry. 3. State the amortisation framework if the hosting contract is for 5 years with an option to extend for 2 more years.
cases.conclusion: Implementation costs of a hosting arrangement that is a service contract follow ASC 350-40: the $450,000 application-development cost is deferred as a prepaid (implementation) asset, not capitalised as software; preliminary-stage, data-conversion and training costs ($180,000) are expensed. Amortised straight-line over the hosting term plus extensions reasonably certain to be exercised.
cases.review_status: provisional: awaiting approval by a qualified accountant
cases.evidence_note: No authorised FASB or PCAOB evidence is held; the expectation is the engineering assistant's reading of US GAAP / PCAOB practice and is not source-verified.

cases.topic: US GAAP revenue with right of return
cases.question: Multi-Element Revenue Recognition with Right of Return (ASC 606). On December 15, 2026, Echo Tech sells 1,000 devices to a distributor for $200 each with a 90-day right of return. Historical returns are 4%; each device costs $110. On December 28 the estimated return rate is revised to 10% before the books close. 1. Calculate the revenue and the refund liability at December 31, 2026. 2. Determine the asset for the right to recover returned products. 3. Draft the December 2026 journal entries.
cases.conclusion: At the revised 10% return rate: revenue $180,000, refund liability $20,000, right-of-return asset $11,000 (100 units at $110), cost of sales $99,000.
cases.review_status: provisional: awaiting approval by a qualified accountant

cases.topic: US GAAP equity method intra-entity profit
cases.question: Equity Method Investment with Intra-Entity Inventory Downstream Sales (ASC 323). Paradigm Corp. holds 40% of Apex Supply. In 2026 Paradigm sells inventory costing $60,000 to Apex for $100,000. At December 31, 2026, 30% of it remains in Apex's inventory. Apex reports net income of $250,000. 1. Calculate the intra-entity unearned profit to eliminate. 2. Determine Paradigm's equity-method income from Apex. 3. Provide the adjusting journal entry.
cases.conclusion: Unrealised profit in Apex's inventory is 30% of $40,000 = $12,000; Paradigm eliminates its 40% share, $4,800. Equity income = 40% × $250,000 − $4,800 = $95,200, recorded in one entry: Dr Investment in Apex $95,200, Cr Equity in earnings $95,200.
cases.review_status: provisional: awaiting approval by a qualified accountant
cases.evidence_note: No authorised FASB or PCAOB evidence is held; the expectation is the engineering assistant's reading of US GAAP / PCAOB practice and is not source-verified.

cases.question: Asset Retirement Obligations with Timing Shifts (ASC 410-20). On January 1, 2023, Vertex Energy built a platform it must dismantle after 10 years. Estimated cost $500,000, credit-adjusted risk-free rate 6% (PV factor 0.5584), initial ARO $279,200. On December 31, 2026 (after 4 years of accretion and straight-line depreciation) the estimated cost falls to $400,000; the current credit-adjusted rate is 5% (6-year PV factor 0.7462). 1. Carrying value of the ARO immediately before the adjustment. 2. The adjustment under ASC 410-20. 3. The impact on the capitalised asset.
cases.conclusion: Before the change the ARO is $279,200 × 1.06^4 ≈ $352,484. A downward revision is discounted at the original 6% rate, not the current 5%: $400,000 ÷ 1.06^6 ≈ $281,984, a decrease of ≈ $70,499 taken against the asset's carrying amount, not recognised as a gain.
cases.review_status: provisional: awaiting approval by a qualified accountant
cases.evidence_note: No authorised FASB or PCAOB evidence is held; the expectation is the engineering assistant's reading of US GAAP / PCAOB practice and is not source-verified.

cases.topic: US GAAP cash flow hedge of a forecast purchase
cases.question: Derivatives & Cash Flow Hedges for Forecasted Inventory Purchases (ASC 815). On October 1, 2026, Horizon Import hedges a forecast purchase of copper on February 1, 2027 with a futures contract qualifying as a cash flow hedge. On December 31, 2026 the contract's fair value rises by $45,000. On February 1, 2027 the copper is bought at spot and the contract settles for a cumulative gain of $60,000. The inventory is sold in March 2027. 1. Journal entry at December 31, 2026. 2. Entries at settlement. 3. Where and when the deferred gains are reclassified.
cases.conclusion: Dr Derivative asset $45,000, Cr OCI $45,000 at year end; a further $15,000 to OCI and cash settlement of $60,000 in February. Under US GAAP the $60,000 stays in AOCI (no basis adjustment to inventory, which is the IFRS 9 approach) and is reclassified to cost of sales when the inventory is sold in March 2027.
cases.review_status: provisional: awaiting approval by a qualified accountant
cases.evidence_note: No authorised FASB or PCAOB evidence is held; the expectation is the engineering assistant's reading of US GAAP / PCAOB practice and is not source-verified.

cases.topic: US GAAP debt with detachable warrants
cases.question: Complex Debt Issuance with Detachable Stock Warrants (ASC 470-20). On January 1, 2026, Nova Corporation issues $3,000,000 par, 7%, 10-year bonds at 102. Each $1,000 bond carries 20 detachable warrants. Ex-warrant the bonds trade at 96 ($2,880,000); the warrants trade at $3 each (60,000 × $3 = $180,000). 1. Allocate the proceeds by relative fair value. 2. Calculate the discount or premium. 3. Provide the journal entry.
cases.conclusion: Proceeds $3,060,000 allocated by relative fair value: bonds $2,880,000, warrants $180,000 (to additional paid-in capital). Discount on the bonds $120,000. Dr Cash $3,060,000, Dr Discount $120,000, Cr Bonds payable $3,000,000, Cr APIC – warrants $180,000.

cases.question: Lease Classifications – Lessee Finance Lease Amortization (ASC 842). On January 1, 2026, Quantum Labs leases machinery for 5 years, no renewal options. Annual payments of $90,000 are due at the start of each year. Economic life 5 years; implicit rate 8%; the present value of the remaining 4 payments at 8% is $298,991. It is a finance lease. 1. Initial ROU asset and lease liability. 2. 2026 interest expense and ROU amortisation. 3. Journal entries at inception and at the first year end.
cases.conclusion: ROU asset and liability $388,991 ($90,000 paid at inception plus $298,991). 2026 interest = 8% × $298,991 = $23,919.28; amortisation = $388,991 ÷ 5 = $77,798.20.

cases.topic: US GAAP deferred tax valuation allowance
cases.question: Income Tax Valuation Allowances for Net Operating Losses (ASC 740). At December 31, 2026, Vanguard Biotech has a gross deferred tax asset of $800,000 from NOLs. It is more likely than not that only $300,000 will be realised. No allowance was recorded before. The tax rate is 21%. 1. The valuation allowance adjustment. 2. How it flows through the income statement. 3. The journal entry.
cases.conclusion: Valuation allowance $500,000 ($800,000 − $300,000), recognised through deferred income tax expense: Dr Deferred tax expense $500,000, Cr Valuation allowance $500,000. The 21% rate is not applied again to an amount already stated as a tax asset.

cases.question: Segment Reporting Allocation Anomalies (ASC 280). Titan Conglomerate allocates shared overhead by ERP: Segment X overhead $1,400,000, assets $12,000,000; Segment Y overhead $900,000, assets $7,000,000; Segment Z overhead $200,000, assets $3,000,000. $600,000 of Segment X's allocation is central financing cost not used by the CODM to assess Segment X. 1. Adjustments to the segment profit measure. 2. Whether unallocated items must be reconciled. 3. The asset test threshold.
cases.conclusion: The segment measure is the one the CODM uses, so the $600,000 of financing cost is excluded from Segment X's reported profit and shown as an unallocated reconciling item; totals of segment profit and assets are reconciled to the consolidated amounts. A segment is reportable under the asset test at 10% of combined segment assets: 10% × $22,000,000 = $2,200,000.
cases.review_status: provisional: awaiting approval by a qualified accountant
cases.evidence_note: No authorised FASB or PCAOB evidence is held; the expectation is the engineering assistant's reading of US GAAP / PCAOB practice and is not source-verified.

cases.question: Audit Sampling Anomaly Evaluation. An auditor tests 45 disbursement approvals (non-statistical; tolerable deviation rate 7%, expected 1.5%) and finds 2 deviations where invoice validation was bypassed. Management says both occurred during 2 days when the control officer was in hospital and asks the auditor to treat them as an isolated anomaly and conclude the control is effective. 1. Evaluate management's argument under PCAOB guidance. 2. Calculate the sample deviation rate. 3. Propose further audit steps.
cases.conclusion: Sample deviation rate 2 ÷ 45 ≈ 4.4%, well above the 1.5% expected, leaving little allowance for sampling risk against the 7% tolerable rate. A deviation is evaluated as a deviation; the reason it occurred (a temporary clerk) is evidence of a control gap during absences, not grounds to exclude it. Further work: extend testing (including the absence period), test compensating controls, consider the effect on assessed control risk and substantive procedures.
cases.review_status: provisional: awaiting approval by a qualified accountant
cases.evidence_note: No authorised FASB or PCAOB evidence is held; the expectation is the engineering assistant's reading of US GAAP / PCAOB practice and is not source-verified.
